Then K∞(φ, α)/K is an abelian extension if and only if the pair (φ, α) is K ab-conjugate to the pair (ψ, β) occurring in one of the following two families of examples: (i) ψ(x) = xd and β = ζ, a root of unity in K. (ii) ψ(x) = Td(x) is the d-th Chebyshev polynomial and β = ζ + ζ −1, where ζ is a root of unity in K. It is well-known that any iterate of an Eisenstein polynomial in Z[x] is again Eisenstein, so the pair (φ(x), 0) is stable whenever φ(x) ∈Z[x] is Eisenstein. In particular, B0(L) ≥CK,D > 0. This result generalizes a result of Amoroso and Dvornicich [2000], which states that h(α) ≥(log 5)/12 for all nonzero, nonroot of unity α ∈Qab. In particular, B0(Qab) ≥(log 5)/12. For our purposes, another useful result from the paper [Amoroso and Dvornicich 2000] is the following. For each k ≥1, let ζk be a primitive k-th root of unity in C, and let µk be the group of all k-th roots of unity in C. Let µ2∞= S m≥1 µ2m; thus Q(µ2∞) = S m≥1 Q(ζ2m).
